description:
Plan: Break Apart App.tsx (1071 Lines) for Concurrency
Current Structure (bert-viz/src/App.tsx read fully):
- State (50+ vars): useState for viewModel/projects/filters/chat/sessions/UI (zoom/dark/scroll/editing). LocalStorage sync.
- Effects/Callbacks (20+): IPC fetchProjectViewModel (debounced 150ms), event listeners (beadsUpdated), keydown, scroll sync, init/load.
- Memos/Computes: flattenTree, ganttLayout (150 lines: positions/connectors), stats.
- Renders: Navigation/Header/Sidebar/WBSTreeList/GanttBar/Skeleton/ChatDialog. Heavy inline logic (toggleNode, handleScroll).
- Props/Children: Self-contained god-component.
Why Too Big? Tight coupling: Filter→IPC→re-render all. No modularity → hard concurrent features (e.g., Chat PR breaks Gantt).
Split Opportunities (Prioritized for Concurrency):
| Slice | Lines/Responsibility | Extract To | Benefits/Concurrent PR |
|-------|----------------------|------------|-------------------------|
| Project Core (~400 lines) | viewModel/fetch/loadData/beads/flattenTree/ganttLayout/WBS+Gantt renders/scroll sync/filters/zoom/stats | <ProjectViewProvider store={projectStore}> <ProjectView /> </ProjectViewProvider> + stores/useProjectStore.ts | Independent perf tweaks (e.g., caching PR). PR1. |
| Chat/Session (~150 lines) | sessionsByBead/ChatDialog/isChatOpen/persona/task/beadId | <ChatProvider store={chatStore}> <ChatDialog /> </ChatProvider> + stores/useChatStore.ts + contexts/ChatContext.tsx | Chat features (multi-session) isolated. PR2. |
| UI/Layout (~200 lines) | Header/Sidebar/Navigation/dark/editing/create/save/keyboard | <UIProvider store={uiStore}> <Layout /> </UIProvider> + stores/useUIStore.ts (sidebarOpen/selectedBead/editForm) | Theme/UI PRs concurrent. PR3. |
| Global Init/Events (~150 lines) | useEffect init/loadProjects/onBeadsUpdated/keydown/localStorage | providers/AppProviders.tsx (wrap roots) + hooks/useGlobalEvents.ts | Infra changes don't touch views. PR4. |
| Utils/Memos | flattenTree/toggleNode/expandAll | hooks/useProjectUtils.ts + hooks/useGanttLayout.ts | Reusable, test independently. |
High-Level Refactor Plan (4 Concurrent PRs, Merge Parallel):
1. Prep (Shared, 1 PR): npm i zustand (check package.json—React19/Vite ok). Create src/stores/index.ts.
2. PR1: ProjectStore + ProjectView (useProjectStore: viewModel/filters/zoom/loadData/ganttLayout).
   - Extract: <ProjectView /> owns WBS/Gantt/scroll.
   - Concurrent: Others work Chat/UI.
3. PR2: ChatStore + ChatProvider (useChatStore: sessions/chat state/IPC).
   - Lazy-load React.lazy(ChatDialog).
4. PR3: UIStore + Layout (useUIStore: editing/sidebar/dark/keybinds).
5. PR4: Orchestrate App.tsx → 100 lines: <AppProviders><ProjectView><ChatProvider>...</ChatProvider></ProjectView></AppProviders>.
   - Global events to custom hook.
Migration Steps (Safe, Incremental):
1. Create stores/useProjectStore.ts:
export useProjectStore = create((set,get) => ({
  viewModel: null, filters: {...}, actions: {loadData: async() => ...}
}));
2. App.tsx: const projectStore = useProjectStore(); → hoist to Provider.
3. Extract <ProjectView useProjectStore /> → test in isolation.
4. Remove from App.tsx → CI lint/typecheck.
Tradeoffs:
- Zustand: Lightweight (no Context hell), devtools. Alt: Context+Reducer (no deps).
- Concurrency: 4 PRs → merge via branches (feature/project-view, feature/chat-store).
- Risks: IPC race (use abortController). Test: Vitest mocks.
- Perf: No regression (memos stay).

description: Replace fragile component-level state management with Zustand store for sessions. Fixes timing issues with event listeners, eliminates duplicate state management logic, and provides single source of truth for session data.
design:
## Current Problems
- Multiple components manage session state independently (App.tsx, SessionList)
- Each component sets up own event listeners (timing issues, duplication)
- Events from Rust not reliably reaching components
- No single source of truth for session data

## Zustand Solution
- Single store manages all session state
- One event listener in store (no timing conflicts)
- Components subscribe to store (no event handling in UI)
- Clear separation: store = data, components = UI

## Implementation
1. Install Zustand dependency
2. Create stores/sessionStore.ts
3. Migrate App.tsx to use store
4. Migrate SessionList to use store
5. Remove duplicate event listeners
6. Test event delivery works

## Files Affected
- package.json (add zustand)
- src/stores/sessionStore.ts (new)
- src/App.tsx (use store instead of local state)
- src/components/session/SessionList.tsx (use store)

## Benefits
- Single source of truth
- Better modularity (state separate from UI)
- Easier testing (mock store)
- Fixes timing issues
- No duplicate logic

description: Selecting a different chat session blanks the UX because we were using the current dialog's bead_id instead of the target session's bead_id when loading history.
notes:
## Root Cause
When switching sessions, `handleSessionSwitch` was calling:
```typescript
loadSessionHistory(targetSessionId, beadId || '')
```

This used the current dialog's `beadId` prop (from the original session), not the target session's `bead_id`. Since each session has its own bead and history directory (`~/.bp6/sessions/<bead_id>`), this caused:
1. Wrong directory lookup
2. No history found
3. Blank messages array
4. Empty UI

## Fix
Changed callback signatures to pass both `sessionId` and `beadId`:
- `onSessionSelect: (sessionId: string, beadId: string) => void`
- `handleSessionSwitch(targetSessionId: string, targetBeadId: string)`
- SessionItem now passes `session.bead_id` along with `session.session_id`

Now loads history from correct directory using target session's bead_id.

## Files Modified
- ChatDialog.tsx: Updated handleSessionSwitch signature
- SessionList.tsx: Updated onSessionSelect prop type  
- SessionItem.tsx: Pass both session_id and bead_id to onSelect

## Testing
- Frontend build successful
- TypeScript compilation passes
title: Fix session switch using wrong bead_id (blanks UX)

close_reason: Implemented debounced scroll-to-bottom on initial PTY data load. Terminal now waits 200ms after data stops flowing, then jumps directly to most recent output instead of scrolling through entire buffer. User no longer sees disorienting scroll animation on initialization.
description:
When the terminal is resized or initialized, the display scrolls through the entire buffer from the beginning, which is disorienting. The buffer should populate backwards from most recent to oldest, keeping the user's current position stable.

**Observed Behavior:**
- On resize/init, terminal scrolls from the very beginning of the buffer
- User loses their place in the output
- Disorienting scroll animation through all content

**Expected Behavior:**
- Terminal shows most recent output by default
- Buffer populates backwards (recent → old) without visible scrolling
- User position remains stable during resize
- OR: Jump directly to end of buffer without scrolling through it

**Options to Consider:**
1. Auto-scroll to bottom after resize/init
2. Preserve scroll position during resize
3. Initialize with buffer already populated at bottom
4. Disable scroll animation during population

**Investigation Areas:**
- Terminal.tsx: xterm.js scrolling behavior during write()
- Check if there's a scrollToBottom() or similar API
- Review xterm.js options for scroll behavior
- PTY reader thread: how output is emitted during initialization
design:
Solution: Debounced scroll-to-bottom after initial PTY data load.

Implementation:
- Added initialLoadRef to track first-time data loading
- Added scrollTimeoutRef for debounced scroll
- On each pty-data event during initial load, reset 200ms timeout
- When data stops flowing, call terminal.scrollToBottom()
- Prevents watching buffer fill, jumps directly to most recent output

Location: Terminal.tsx lines 33-34, 94-110, 129-132
notes:
Changes in Terminal.tsx:
- Added initialLoadRef (boolean) and scrollTimeoutRef (number)
- Modified pty-data listener to debounce scroll on initial load
- After 200ms of no data, scrolls to bottom and marks initial load complete
- Cleanup includes clearing scroll timeout

The goal is an event-driven orchestration foundation that eliminates polling, file-based IPC, and daemon lock contention — and provides the substrate for live agent handoffs, human question queues, and real-time work allocation. This is a design-first epic: ideas to be developed before coding begins.
notes:
## Emerging Direction — Custom MCP Toolset (2026-02-28, exploratory)

NOT a committed decision — capturing the idea for further consideration.

### The option
Drop the beads dependency entirely. Instead of wrapping bd CLI or syncing with beads storage, build a minimal MCP tool surface directly over Restate from the start.

Agents would call MCP tools natively (no bd subprocess, no file parsing). The tool surface is designed for what agents actually need, not inherited from beads' CLI design.

Candidate MCP tool surface (~8 tools):
- create_issue, update_issue, close_issue
- get_ready_work, show_issue, list_issues
- add_dependency, get_blocked

Everything else (export, compact, sync, stats) lives outside MCP as human/UI operations.

### Why this is attractive
- Beads itself is mid-migration (JSONL → Dolt/SQLite) — building on it is building on shifting ground
- Agents talk to MCP natively — cleaner than subprocess + CLI output parsing
- MCP server = additional routes on the axum server already needed for Restate FaaS callbacks
- Removes the git sync story as a blocker (Restate journal is the audit trail for single-user)

### Why it's not baked yet
- Significant break from current agent workflows
- git-backed collaboration story (bd sync) is unresolved
- Agents are currently trained on bd commands — refactor scope unknown
- No validation that the 8-tool surface covers all real agent use cases
title: Replace beads with native event-driven orchestration layer

description:
PTY (terminal mode) output is currently ephemeral — nothing is written to the session JSONL log. This means any work done in terminal mode is lost from the session record, breaking the process improvement review workflow.

## Problem
- Session JSONL logs capture chat messages and agent chunks, but nothing from PTY mode
- Switching back from PTY to chat shows no record of what happened in the terminal
- Process improvement reviews cannot inspect terminal activity

## Desired outcome
1. PTY output is appended to the session JSONL as a new event type (e.g. LogEventType::PtyOutput)
2. When reviewing a session log (get_session_history), PTY blocks appear in chronological order
3. When switching back from PTY to chat, the UI shows the captured PTY output as a collapsible 'Terminal session' block in the message history

## Implementation notes
- The PTY reader thread in spawn_pty_for_session already has the output — it just needs to write it to the SessionLogger in addition to emitting pty-data events
- Need a new LogEventType::PtyOutput variant (or reuse Chunk with a pty flag in metadata)
- get_session_history needs to reconstruct PtyOutput blocks into ConversationMessage entries
- Frontend ChatDialog needs a new message bubble type to render terminal output (monospace, collapsible)
- Should buffer/batch PTY writes (e.g. flush every 500ms or on PTY close) to avoid excessive JSONL churn

## Scope
Covers agent PTY mode (spawn_pty_for_session). Project shell (spawn_project_shell) is separate and lower priority.
title: Log PTY/terminal output to session JSONL for process review

description:
## Overview
Bead detail modal with read/write capability, replacing the current sidebar inline editing approach. Triggered by repurposing the existing show/hide sidebar button on the zoom/reset control.

## Design

### Trigger
- Repurpose the existing show/hide sidebar button → show/hide bead detail modal
- Modal shows detail for the currently selected bead (one modal, always current selection)

### Modal Layout
- Approximately 1/3 window width/height
- Two modes toggled within the same modal window:

**View Mode** (default):
- Client-side markdown rendering of each bead field
- Clean, human-readable — no raw syntax visible

**Edit Mode** (toggle from view):
- Structured form fields per section (title, description, acceptance, design, notes)
- Pre-populated from bead JSON
- Save triggers bd update with changed fields only
- Returns to view mode on save

### Data Flow
- Modal opens → fetch bead JSON (one Tauri IPC call, existing command)
- View mode → client-side markdown render (marked.js or equivalent)
- Edit mode → structured form fields, no backend involvement until save
- Save → bd update IPC call with changed fields only

## Why Client-Side Rendering
- Avoids IPC round-trips on view/edit toggle — instant switching
- Bead JSON fetched once on open, renderer is trivial cost
- Edit mode uses structured fields, not raw markdown — no need to parse markdown back into fields on save

## Relationship to bp6-p41v.39
- bp6-p41v.39 (Bead::to_markdown()) is for agent session prompt injection only
- This modal does its own client-side rendering — separate concern, not dependent on p41v.39

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Show/hide sidebar button repurposed to show/hide bead detail modal
- [ ] Modal opens to ~1/3 window width/height
- [ ] View mode renders markdown cleanly — no raw syntax visible
- [ ] Edit mode shows structured form fields pre-populated from bead data
- [ ] Save updates only changed fields via bd update
- [ ] Modal always reflects currently selected bead
- [ ] Single modal instance — no stacking
title: Enhanced Bead Detail View/Edit with Markdown Support

description:
## Issues
1. switchActiveSession sends sessionId (camelCase) but Rust expects session_id (snake_case)
2. SessionInfo TypeScript interface uses snake_case but Rust serializes with camelCase
3. This causes:
   - Session switching to fail: 'missing required key sessionId'
   - Runtime display to show NaN: created_at is undefined

## Evidence
Console errors:
- Failed to switch session: command switch_active_session missing required key sessionId
- Session runtime shows 'NaNm NaNs'

## Root Cause
Rust SessionInfo has #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] which serializes:
- session_id → sessionId
- bead_id → beadId  
- created_at → createdAt

But TypeScript interface expects snake_case fields.

## Fix
Update api.ts to use camelCase parameter names and interface fields to match Rust serialization.
design:
## Root Causes

1. **SessionInfo field name mismatch**: Rust serializes with #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] but TypeScript interface used snake_case
   - Rust: sessionId, beadId, createdAt, backendId  
   - TypeScript (old): session_id, bead_id, created_at, backend_id
   - Result: TypeScript received camelCase but tried to access snake_case → undefined values → NaN

2. **Runtime calculation bug**: formatSessionRuntime expected milliseconds but Rust sends seconds
   - elapsed = Date.now() (ms) - createdAt (seconds treated as ms) → wrong calculation
   - Fixed: Convert Date.now() to seconds before subtraction

3. **Tauri auto-converts parameters**: Rust snake_case parameters automatically become camelCase in JavaScript
   - Rust: session_id: String → JavaScript: sessionId
   - Must send camelCase parameter names in invoke() calls

## Fixes

1. Updated TypeScript SessionInfo interface to use camelCase field names
2. Fixed formatSessionRuntime to handle seconds correctly  
3. Updated all component references from snake_case to camelCase
4. Fixed null handling for optional beadId field
5. Kept Tauri invoke calls using camelCase (auto-converted by Tauri)
title: Fix session switching parameter name mismatches

design:
# AI Test Engineer Role Template

## Role Overview
**Purpose**: Execute end-to-end manual testing of system features in staging environments, documenting the complete test process, discovering and resolving blockers, and producing production-readiness reports.

**Key Capabilities**:
- Pre-test system audits (schema validation, function dependency checks)
- Blocker identification and bug tracking
- End-to-end flow validation
- Test report generation with visual documentation (sequence diagrams)

---

## Entry Criteria
**Required Inputs**:
1. Feature specification
2. Environment access (staging/test)
3. Test user accounts
4. Success criteria (ACs)
5. System context (schema dumps, migrations)

**Prerequisites**: Feature implementation complete, migrations applied, test data available.

---

## Testing Process

### Phase 1: Pre-Test Audit (CRITICAL)
**Activities**:
1. **Schema Validation**: Dump schema, verify function calls and table names.
2. **Dependency Audit**: Trace flow from trigger to completion.
3. **Migration Verification**: Check applied status and consistency.
4. **Bug Discovery**: Create bug issues for EACH blocker (P0). DO NOT attempt to fix.

### Phase 2: Test Execution
**Activities**:
1. **Environment Setup**: User login and role verification.
2. **Step-by-Step Execution**: Document each step with ✅/❌.
3. **Data Validation**: Query DB to verify state changes and accuracy.
4. **Edge Case Testing**: Zero values, null data, concurrency.

### Phase 3: Report Generation
**Activities**:
1. **Create Sequence Diagram**: Mermaid syntax flow trigger → processing → completion.
2. **Document Test Results**: Executive summary (PASS/FAIL), log, and AC validation table.
3. **Generate Recommendations**: Production readiness and monitoring advice.
4. **Link Issues**: Reference all related bug IDs.

---

## Deliverables
1. **Test Report (Markdown)**: Saved to .
2. **Bug Issues**: In issue tracker, linked to feature.
3. **Updated Test Task**: Notes updated with report link.

---

## Anti-Patterns
- Skipping Phase 1 Audit.
- Fixing bugs during test (Role is to TEST, not develop).
- Ignoring schema dumps in favor of migration files.
- Verbose SQL dumps instead of concise status tables.
title: Guided Testing & QA Persona

PROBLEM
When an agent is running on a task, the user cannot easily tell what it is doing or open its chat window from the WBS. They must guess which session corresponds to which bead and navigate back through the nav menu to find and open it. The WBS row should make active sessions immediately obvious and accessible with a single click.

WHAT TO BUILD

1. HOVER POPOVER on SessionIndicator
   When the user hovers the session indicator dot on a WBS row, show a small popover containing:
   - Persona icon + persona/role name (e.g. '🧑‍💻 flutter-specialist')
   - Task name (from SessionInfo.task)
   - 'Click to open chat' affordance (cursor pointer, subtle CTA)
   - OPTIONAL / NICE-TO-HAVE: most recent message preview (already in session history — do not implement if it complicates v1)
   Multiple sessions on same bead: list each one in the popover as separate rows.

2. CLICK TO OPEN CHAT
   Clicking the SessionIndicator should call createSessionWindow(session.sessionId).
   This opens the pop-out chat window for that session (or focuses it if already open — createSessionWindow handles this).
   If multiple sessions on same bead: single session → open immediately. Multiple sessions → popover lists each; user clicks the specific one.

WHAT NOT TO CHANGE
- Do not remove or replace the existing nav-based session switcher
- Do not change WBSTreeItem click behaviour (that selects the bead, unrelated)
- Do not change the visual indicator itself (pulsing dot + persona icon + count badge is fine)

DATA FLOW (read this before touching anything)
- App.tsx line 102: sessionsByBead = useMemo(() => groupSessionsByBead(sessions), [sessions])
- sessionsByBead is passed as prop to WBSTreeList (lines 1421, 1512) → WBSTreeItem (line 161) → SessionIndicator (line 108)
- SessionInfo type is in src/api.ts line 167. Key fields: sessionId, persona, role, task, status
- createSessionWindow(sessionId) is in src/api.ts line 393 — already imported in App.tsx line 22
- Sessions with status === 'running' are the active ones (SessionIndicator already filters for this)

FILES TO CHANGE
1. src/components/shared/SessionIndicator.tsx  — add onSessionClick prop + hover popover
2. src/components/wbs/WBSTreeItem.tsx          — add onSessionClick prop, pass through to SessionIndicator
3. src/components/wbs/WBSTreeList (same file)  — add onSessionClick prop, pass through to WBSTreeItem
4. src/App.tsx                                 — pass onSessionClick={createSessionWindow} into WBSTreeList at lines 1421 and 1512

PROP INTERFACE CHANGE
SessionIndicator currently:
  interface SessionIndicatorProps { sessions: SessionInfo[]; className?: string; }
Add:
  onSessionClick?: (sessionId: string) => void;

WBSTreeItem currently has onStartSession?: (beadId, persona) => void — add:
  onSessionClick?: (sessionId: string) => void;

WBSTreeList — same addition, pass through.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES
- Popover: use a simple CSS hover group (Tailwind group-hover) or a small useState isHovered — do NOT pull in a third-party popover library
- Position popover above or to the right of the indicator to avoid being clipped by the row
- The indicator sits at line 108 of WBSTreeItem inside a flex-1 div; the WBS row is 40px tall — popover needs z-index and absolute positioning
- Keep it simple: this is a small focused change, not a redesign

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Hovering the session indicator on a WBS row shows a popover with persona name and task
- [ ] Clicking the indicator (single session) immediately opens/focuses the chat window
- [ ] Clicking a session row in the popover (multiple sessions) opens that specific chat window
- [ ] No changes to bead-row click behaviour (still selects the bead)
- [ ] TypeScript compiles clean (tsc --noEmit passes)
- [ ] Works in both main window WBS and session window WBS

close_reason: Duplicate of bp6-p9g1. Fixed by killing existing process before spawning new one when switching between CHAT and CLI modes.
description:
When switching from Chat mode to CLI/Terminal mode in an active agent session, users encounter:

Error: Session ID <uuid> is already in use.

## Root Cause Analysis

The bug occurs in the PTY spawn workflow (session.rs:1783-1878):

1. User starts session in Chat mode with session_id (UUID)
2. Backend starts CLI process with --session-id <uuid> flag  
3. User clicks 'CLI' button to switch to terminal mode
4. spawn_pty_for_session() is called (line 1783)
5. build_pty_args() passes SAME session_id to Claude CLI (line 1822, claude.rs:55-60)
6. Claude CLI rejects because session_id is already in use by the Chat mode process

## Code Location

- **Primary bug**: bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs:55-60
- **Trigger**: bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs:1822
- **Context**: Session switching flow (Chat → Terminal)

## Expected Behavior

- Switching to CLI mode should either:
  A. Resume the existing session WITHOUT spawning new process, OR
  B. Use a different PTY-specific session identifier

## Current Behavior

- PTY spawn attempts to use same session_id, causing conflict
- Error propagates to frontend CLI window

## Impact

- Prevents users from switching to terminal/CLI mode
- Breaks multi-modal interaction workflow (chat + terminal)
- P2 priority: Workaround is to use separate sessions
design:
## Proposed Fix: Option A (Recommended)

**Use --resume instead of --session-id for PTY mode**

Since the session already exists (started in Chat mode), the PTY should RESUME it, not create a new session with the same ID.

### Implementation

In `claude.rs:55-60`, change `build_pty_args()`:

```rust
fn build_pty_args(&self, session_id: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        "--resume".to_string(),
        session_id.to_string(),  // Resume existing session
        "--dangerously-skip-permissions".to_string(),
    ]
}
```

### Testing
1. Start session in Chat mode
2. Click CLI button
3. Verify terminal opens and resumes conversation
4. Send messages via both Chat and CLI
5. Verify no session ID conflict

---

## Alternative: Option B (More Complex)

**Generate separate PTY session ID**

Keep Chat and CLI as separate Claude sessions with different UUIDs, but link them in application state.

### Pros
- Cleaner separation
- Each mode has its own CLI process

### Cons
- More complex state management
- Requires session synchronization
- May confuse conversation history

**Recommendation**: Use Option A (--resume) for simplicity and correctness.
title: Session ID conflict when switching from Chat to CLI mode

description:
# Adaptation Layer — PM Persona Tool Restriction Briefing

## Context

This document captures a planning conversation about tightening tool access for the PM persona in the adaptation layer. The goal is to prevent AI agents operating in PM mode from taking unilateral actions on specialist systems (database, code, edge functions) while preserving read access needed for grounded decision-making.

## Background — What Went Wrong Today

A PM session (Claude, `participant_v3` branch) was given a bug bead (`WellbeingPassport-9n2.2.22`) describing an empty recommendations dashboard. The PM correctly diagnosed the root cause (RPC filtering on `'approved'` — not a valid `verification_status` value per the DB check constraint) but then:

1. Called `mcp__supabase__apply_migration` directly — dropped and recreated a live database function
2. Tried to write local migration files (created duplicates, wrong paths)
3. Closed the bead prematurely
4. Made a mess of the migration history that required manual cleanup

The PM persona had full MCP tool access. The system prompt said not to do this. The agent did it anyway. **Instructions are not guardrails.**

## The Adaptation Layer Architecture

The adaptation layer:
- Invokes the agent CLI tool (currently Claude Code)
- Pipes via `--json` and stdin/stdout/stderr
- Uses session IDs mapped to `{ bead_id, persona, task }` tuples
- Supports multiplexing — same bead ID can have concurrent sessions with different personas
- Logs the full conversation thread as it passes through stdio — full audit trail of every tool call
- Personas are stateless per session ID — conversation continuity within a session, fresh start across sessions
- Context is established at session start by traversing the bead hierarchy (ancestors, peers, children, dependencies)
- Has persona+task templates that control system prompt and (currently) MCP config

## The Fix — What Needs to Be Built

### 1. Per-Persona MCP Config Selection

The adaptation layer already controls CLI invocation. It should select an MCP config file based on persona:

```
persona: product_manager  →  --mcp-config pm-mcp.json
persona: developer        →  --mcp-config dev-mcp.json
persona: ...              →  --mcp-config ...
```

The `--mcp-config` flag needs to be validated against the Claude Code CLI (`claude --help | grep mcp`) — the flag name was not confirmed during this conversation.

### 2. PM MCP Config — Tool Allowlist

The PM persona should have access to:

**Supabase (read-only):**
- `mcp__supabase__list_tables`
- `mcp__supabase__list_extensions`
- `mcp__supabase__list_migrations`
- `mcp__supabase__get_logs`
- `mcp__supabase__get_advisors`
- `mcp__supabase__generate_typescript_types`
- `mcp__supabase__execute_sql` — with SELECT-only enforcement (see below)

**Dart/Flutter (read-only):**
- `mcp__dart__analyze_files`
- `mcp__dart__hover`
- `mcp__dart__resolve_workspace_symbol`
- `mcp__dart__read_package_uris`

**Local filesystem (read-only):**
- `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`

**Beads (full access):**
- All `bd` commands via Bash — scoped to beads CLI only

**Explicitly denied:**
- `mcp__supabase__apply_migration`
- `mcp__supabase__deploy_edge_function`
- `mcp__supabase__create_branch`, `delete_branch`, `merge_branch`, `reset_branch`, `rebase_branch`
- `Write`, `Edit`, `NotebookEdit`
- `Bash` (except beads CLI — see Bash scoping below)

### 3. SELECT-Only Enforcement on execute_sql

`execute_sql` cannot be made read-only through config alone — the tool accepts any SQL. The adaptation layer sits on the stdio pipe and can inspect JSON tool calls before forwarding them.

For PM sessions, intercept `mcp__supabase__execute_sql` tool calls and:
- Allow if the SQL (trimmed, uppercased) starts with SELECT or WITH
- Reject with an explanatory error otherwise

This is the one place where the adaptation layer needs to act as a proxy, not just a config selector.

### 4. Bash Scoping for Beads

The PM persona needs Bash access for beads commands (`bd show`, `bd list`, `bd create`, etc.) but not for general shell access. Options:

- **Allowlist approach**: Intercept Bash tool calls on the pipe, allow only if command starts with `bd `
- **Alternative**: Expose beads as a dedicated MCP server — cleaner separation, removes Bash dependency entirely

## Key Design Principles

1. **Instructions are not guardrails.** No prompt, CLAUDE.md, or system message reliably prevents a capable model from taking an action it has the tools to take. Guardrails must be mechanical.
2. **Tool access is the right control layer.** If a persona can't call a tool, it can't misuse it — model-agnostic by design.
3. **Read access is non-negotiable for PM.** A PM without schema/code read access will hallucinate — worse than the problem being solved.
4. **The stdio audit log is your QA/QC loop.** Every tool call every persona makes is logged — feedback mechanism for tightening templates over time.
5. **Bead hierarchy is the context boundary.** PM traverses ancestors/children/peers/dependencies from the entry bead ID.
6. **Write conflicts on beads are low-priority risk** (~0.01% of interactions). Audit log provides forensics. Not worth solving now.

## Outstanding Questions for the Dev Session

1. Does `claude --help` confirm a `--mcp-config` flag? If not, what is the correct flag name?
2. What is the current MCP config format — standard `.mcp.json` or something custom?
3. How does the adaptation layer currently pass MCP config to the CLI?
4. Is Bash currently unrestricted for all personas, or is there already some filtering?
5. Should beads be migrated to a dedicated MCP server to remove the Bash dependency entirely?

## Files to Look At

- The adaptation layer CLI invocation code — wherever it spawns the agent process
- The current PM persona task template — system prompt and MCP config
- The stdio pipe interception layer — where SELECT-only filtering would be added
design: Instructions-are-not-guardrails principle: tool access is the mechanical control layer. Adaptation layer selects MCP config file at agent spawn time based on persona. Stdio proxy intercepts and validates execute_sql calls (SELECT/WITH prefix check) and optionally Bash calls (bd prefix check). Per-persona config files live alongside persona templates. Beads-as-MCP-server is the preferred long-term solution for Bash scoping.

description: The Gemini CLI no longer starts. On launch, users receive a 'session does not exist' error, making it completely unusable.
design:
Root cause analysis points to a potential breaking change in the Gemini CLI rather than a bug in bp6 code.

Key finding: In session.rs:918, start_agent_session passes a self-generated UUID as the cli_session_id to gemini --resume <uuid> for new sessions. This relies on the Gemini CLI accepting an unknown UUID gracefully (treating it as a 'start with this ID' hint). If a recent Gemini CLI update made --resume strict (hard-failing on unknown session IDs instead of creating a new session), this would cause 'session does not exist' on every new session start.

The slow startup / update-check behaviour may mask this: Gemini may show an update prompt before the session init, making it appear slow rather than broken.

Investigation steps:
1. Check installed Gemini CLI version (gemini --version) and compare against changelog for breaking changes to --resume
2. Test: run gemini --output-format stream-json --yolo --prompt 'hello' directly (no --resume) to confirm if a fresh session works
3. If confirmed: fix in session.rs start_agent_session - do NOT pass session_id as cli_session_id on new session creation (resume=false). Only pass a cli_session_id when resuming an existing session.
title: Gemini CLI fails to start — 'session does not exist' error

description:
Currently, the tool dynamically generates the initial system prompt (persona + task instructions) to establish an agent session, but this prompt is not persisted after the session starts.

**The Idea**:
1. Write the generated initial system prompt to a session-specific file (e.g. /tmp/agent-sessions/session-{id}.md or similar)
2. Optionally, explore whether agent tools (Claude Code, Gemini CLI) support an environment variable to load instructions from a custom file path instead of default CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md — which would load instructions at the infrastructure level rather than the conversation layer
3. Retain these session files as artifacts for after-action review

**Why**:
- Enables prompt engineering feedback loop: input (instructions) + output (result) = reviewable artifact
- Helps identify when instructions are too long/broad and getting context-weighted out mid-session
- QA and QC Engineer personas are prime candidates — they have specific, structured workflows that degrade if instructions are forgotten
- Over time, builds a corpus of 'what works' per persona/task combination

**Context Loss Note**:
- Long sessions risk instructions being pushed far enough back in context that they're effectively lost when needed
- Tightly scoped, persisted per-session files with only what that agent needs is less likely to get diluted than a fat general-purpose prompt
- This doesn't fully solve mid-session context loss, but enables iteration on instruction quality to minimize it

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Initial session prompt is written to a persistent file at session creation time
- [ ] File is retained post-session for review
- [ ] After-action review workflow defined (prompt in, result out, quality assessment)
- [ ] Investigate env var mechanism for CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md custom path support
notes: CLARIFICATION: The persistence/after-action review benefit is simply a logging problem — write the generated prompt to a file before sending it. No env var research or architectural changes needed to get the core value. The env var idea (loading instructions at infrastructure level via custom CLAUDE.md path) is a separate, more speculative concern about *where* instructions load from, not about retaining them. These are two distinct problems that got conflated. Quick win: just log the prompt, keep the file.
title: Persist initial session prompts for QA/QC after-action review and prompt engineering improvement

description:
In long QA/QC test sessions, context compression causes the agent to forget critical role constraints mid-session. Failure modes observed:
1. Forgets role boundary — starts fixing issues instead of just recording them (active codebase damage)
2. Forgets bead hygiene — raises issues incorrectly or against wrong parent epic
3. Forgets test context — loses track of where it is in the procedure

**The Idea**:
Separate the full persona instructions (verbose, likely to get compressed away) from a compact 'never forget' block covering only hard constraints. Hypothesis: compression de-weights long detailed instructions before short sharp ones. A 5-line block of hard constraints may survive where a 200-line persona file doesn't.

**Candidate constraints for QA/QC test manager**:
- NEVER modify code — observe and record only
- ALWAYS raise bugs as child of the active test epic
- ALWAYS follow bead raising format exactly

**Related**:
- bp6-p41v.34 (session prompt persistence / after-action review)
- Short session + handoff model is preferred overall, but long test procedures are a real edge case that needs mitigation

**To investigate**:
- Does compression preferentially drop longer blocks vs. short ones?
- What is the minimum viable constraint set for QA/QC role safety?
- Can the 'never forget' block be injected separately from persona instructions at session start?
notes: Event-driven re-injection (detecting compression on stdio and reinjecting) was also discussed as an alternative mitigation, but depends on compression being reliably detectable as a structured event — unvalidated.
title: Investigate compact 'never forget' constraint block to survive context compression in long test sessions

description:
## Observed Behaviour
When a user closes a chat window that was previously in CLI/terminal mode and then reopens it and switches back to CLI, the tool errors with 'Session already has a PTY'.

## Root Cause
`spawn_pty_for_session` (session.rs:1797) guards against double-spawning with:
```rust
if session.pty_session_id.is_some() {
    return Err("Session already has a PTY".to_string());
}
```
PTY cleanup only happens in `terminate_session` and `stop_agent_session`. Closing a window does NOT call either — so `pty_session_id` survives on the SessionState. Next attempt to spawn a PTY hits the guard and fails.

## Recommended Fix
When a window is closed, if the associated session has an active PTY (`pty_session_id.is_some()`), kill it via `pty_manager.kill()` and clear `session.pty_session_id = None`. This mirrors what `terminate_session` already does.

An alternative is to make `spawn_pty_for_session` idempotent — if a PTY already exists, kill it and respawn — but this is less clean and could mask other lifecycle issues.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Closing a chat window that was in CLI mode cleans up the PTY session
- [ ] Re-opening the window and switching to CLI mode works without error
- [ ] `terminate_session` and `stop_agent_session` behaviour unchanged
title: PTY not cleaned up when chat window is closed, causing 'Session already has a PTY' error on reopen

description:
## Observed Behaviour
While a session is actively streaming, any new chunk arriving immediately scrolls the chat window to the bottom — even if the user has manually scrolled up to read an earlier message. The user cannot read previous output without the view being hijacked back to the bottom.

## Expected Behaviour
Sticky-bottom scroll should be conditional:
- If the user is already at (or near) the bottom → auto-scroll to follow new output
- If the user has scrolled up → do NOT scroll — let new chunks arrive silently and let the user read at their own pace

## Implementation Note
Standard pattern: on each new chunk, check scroll position before deciding whether to auto-scroll.
```
const isAtBottom = container.scrollHeight - container.scrollTop - container.clientHeight < threshold (e.g. 50px)
if (isAtBottom) {
    container.scrollTo({ top: container.scrollHeight })
}
```
Also common to show a 'scroll to bottom' affordance (e.g. a chevron-down button) when the user is scrolled up and new content is arriving, so they know output is being received.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New chunks do not force scroll if user has scrolled above the bottom threshold
- [ ] Auto-scroll resumes naturally if the user scrolls back to the bottom
- [ ] Optional: 'scroll to bottom' button visible when scrolled up and stream is active
notes: Low friction to implement — pure frontend change, no backend involvement.
title: Chat window forcibly scrolls to bottom on new chunk even when user has scrolled up

description:
## Problem
Bead context is currently appended to session prompts as pretty-printed JSON (persona.rs:build_prompt). JSON has significant syntactic overhead (quoted keys, quoted strings, braces, colons) that consumes tokens without adding semantic value for an LLM.

## Solution
Convert bead context serialization from JSON to markdown before injection into the prompt. Markdown is more token-efficient (typically 20-40% fewer tokens for equivalent information) and more natural for LLM reasoning given training data composition.

## Proposed Format
```markdown
# {bead_id} — {title}
**Status**: {status} | **Priority**: {priority} | **Type**: {issue_type}

## Description
{description}

## Acceptance Criteria
{acceptance}

## Design Notes
{design}
```

## Implementation
- Modify `build_prompt_with_persona` in session.rs to serialize bead as markdown instead of JSON
- Or add a `to_markdown()` method to the Bead struct for reuse
- Remove the `Context JSON:` block in `build_prompt` (persona.rs) and replace with a `## Bead Context` markdown section

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bead context injected as markdown, not JSON
- [ ] All relevant bead fields represented (id, title, status, priority, description, acceptance, design, notes)
- [ ] No regression in agent ability to reference bead context during sessions
notes: IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTION: Put serialization on the Bead struct as to_markdown(). Use a generic JSON-to-markdown approach: (1) serialize Bead to serde_json::Value (already derived), (2) pass through a generic JSON→markdown renderer crate, (3) to_markdown() is a thin wrapper. Advantage: new fields added to Bead are automatically reflected in markdown output — no manual field mapping to maintain. CAVEAT: Generic renderers tend to produce mechanical nested-bullet output mirroring JSON structure, which may not be optimal for LLM consumption. Check output quality and consider a light field-ordering/filtering layer on top — e.g. promote title/description/acceptance to top-level headers, suppress empty fields, order by semantic importance rather than struct field order.
title: Convert bead context injection from JSON to markdown in session prompts

description:
Users can add or modify personas by editing files on disk — no Rust recompile or frontend code changes required. The backend parses persona.md frontmatter at startup, builds a typed PersonaConfig registry, and exposes it over IPC. The frontend renders the persona menu dynamically from this config, making it completely persona-agnostic.

WHAT: Replace hardcoded PERSONAS array (Navigation.tsx), PersonaType enum (persona.rs), and string match arms (session.rs) with a filesystem-driven configuration system where each persona directory contains a persona.md with YAML frontmatter defining all display and routing metadata.

WHY: Currently adding a persona requires touching 4+ files across Rust and TypeScript. The specialist/role indirection is a leaky abstraction. The register_defaults() function uses unsafe {} to work around &self immutability — a soundness bug.

SCOPE:
- bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/persona.rs — replace PersonaType enum with String keys
- bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/personas/ — simplify or remove per-persona structs
- bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/templates.rs — add frontmatter parsing at startup
- bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs — remove string→enum match arm
- bert-viz/src/components/layout/Navigation.tsx — remove PERSONAS array, fetch dynamically
- templates/personas/*/persona.md — add YAML frontmatter to each
design:
Architecture: Filesystem-driven persona registration with YAML frontmatter.

FRONTMATTER SCHEMA (persona.md):
  ---
  id: flutter
  label: Flutter Specialist
  icon: 📱
  color: blue
  group: specialist
  tasks:
    - id: chat
      label: Chat
      icon: message-square
    - id: implement
      label: Implement
      icon: terminal
  ---

RUST STARTUP SEQUENCE:
  1. TemplateLoader walks templates/personas/ directories
  2. Parses persona.md frontmatter in each (using serde_yaml or gray_matter crate)
  3. Builds Vec<PersonaConfig> with id, label, icon, color, group, tasks
  4. PersonaRegistry keyed by String (persona id) — no enum
  5. New Tauri command: get_personas() -> Result<Vec<PersonaConfig>, String>

FRONTEND:
  - On mount, call get_personas() and store result in state
  - Navigation renders PersonaMenu from this data
  - handleSelectTask unchanged in behavior: passes persona id + task id to onOpenChat
  - Icon mapping: maintain a small iconName→LucideComponent map in frontend (icons cant be in JSON)

SPECIALIST FLATTENING:
  - Remove SpecialistPersona struct (or reduce to shared default impl)
  - flutter/, tauri/, supabase-db/, supabase-edge/ become peer top-level directories
  - Session dispatch: persona_id IS the template directory — no role field needed
  - onOpenChat role parameter becomes redundant and can be dropped

UNSAFE FIX:
  - register_defaults() replaced by startup filesystem scan
  - PersonaRegistry built from parsed frontmatter, no unsafe mutation

MIGRATION PATH:
  1. Add frontmatter to existing persona.md files
  2. Add serde_yaml to Cargo.toml
  3. Implement frontmatter parser in TemplateLoader
  4. Implement get_personas() Tauri command
  5. Replace PersonaType enum with String keys throughout
  6. Update frontend to fetch and render dynamically
  7. Remove specialist wrapper — rename directories as needed
title: Data-Driven Persona System: Filesystem-Defined Personas with YAML Frontmatter

close_reason: Fixed session ID conflict by using --resume instead of --session-id for PTY mode and increasing termination delays from 100ms to 500ms. This gives Claude enough time to release the session lock when switching between CHAT and CLI modes.
description:
Switching from CHAT to CLI when useing claude gives this:

Error: Session ID e0f0f4c2-a7ba-421c-be86-da62a672bf09 is already in use.
design:
ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS:

Current approach in spawn_pty_for_session:
1. Kill chat process (SIGINT then SIGKILL after 50ms)
2. Wait 100ms
3. Spawn PTY with --session-id <cli_session_id>

PROBLEM: Even after killing the process, Claude's session lock persists. The PTY spawn uses:
  claude --session-id <id> --dangerously-skip-permissions

But the session <id> is still locked internally by Claude, even though the process is dead.

PROPOSED SOLUTIONS:

Option A: Increase delay significantly (500-1000ms)
  - Simple but unreliable (arbitrary timing)
  - Still might fail under load

Option B: Use --resume instead of --session-id for PTY
  - Currently PTY uses: --session-id <id>
  - Should use: --resume <id> (like chat mode does)
  - This might handle session handoff better

Option C: Poll for session availability
  - Try spawning with timeout/retry
  - Increase delay progressively (100ms, 200ms, 500ms)
  - Fail after max attempts

Option D: Don't reuse session ID
  - Create new PTY session, lose history (BAD UX)

RECOMMENDED: Try Option B first (use --resume for PTY), fallback to Option C if needed.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE:

Changes Made:
1. **bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/backends/claude.rs:57**
   - Changed PTY args from `--session-id` to `--resume`
   - This should handle session handoff more gracefully

2. **bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs:1806**
   - Increased delay from 100ms to 500ms in spawn_pty_for_session
   - Added logging: "Waiting for session lock to be released..."

3. **bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs:1934**
   - Increased delay from 100ms to 500ms in detach_pty_from_session
   - Added logging: "Waiting for session lock to be released..."

Rationale:
- Using --resume instead of --session-id should be more robust for session handoff
- 500ms delay gives Claude enough time to fully release the session lock
- Symmetrical delays in both directions (CHAT→CLI and CLI→CHAT)

Build Status: ✅ Compiles successfully (cargo check passed)

TESTING REQUIRED:
1. Restart tauri dev (it should auto-rebuild on file change)
2. Start a chat session
3. Switch to CLI mode (should work without "Session ID already in use" error)
4. Switch back to CHAT mode
5. Repeat multiple times to verify stability
title: Claude CLI - Cannot Open CLI in chat window anymore.

description:
File watcher is created once at app startup and never updates when switching projects.

Current Behavior:
- Watcher created in setup() on line 494-543
- Uses std::mem::forget() so it lives forever
- When user switches projects, get_beads() reads new project
- But watcher still monitors old project path

Result:
- UI doesn't update when new project's file changes
- UI might update when old project's file changes (wrong!)

Solution:
- Store watcher in app state (AppHandle)
- On project switch, drop old watcher and create new one
- OR: Use event listener to dynamically update watched path
- OR: Move watcher setup to open_project command

Acceptance Criteria:
- Switching projects updates the file watcher
- UI responds to changes in current project only
- No memory leaks from old watchers
notes:
## Current Implementation Issue

The approach of using Arc<Mutex<Option<PathBuf>>> to update watch_target won't work because:

1. Watcher watches specific parent directory with `watcher.watch(&parent_path, ...)`
2. When project changes, we update watch_target but watcher still watches old parent_path
3. New project's file events won't reach the watcher callback

## Proper Solution Needed

Need to actually recreate the watcher, which requires:
1. Tauri managed state to store watcher
2. Drop old watcher when project changes  
3. Create new watcher for new project's parent directory

This is complex - may need to use crossbeam channels or refactor significantly.


## Interim Workaround

**User Action:** Restart the app after switching projects  
- File watcher initializes on startup for current project
- Switching projects doesn't recreate the watcher
- Restarting the app fixes this

## Long-term Solution

Requires significant refactoring:
1. Use Tauri managed state to store watcher
2. Drop old watcher when project changes  
3. Create new watcher with new parent_path
4. Handle watcher lifecycle properly

Complexity: High
Priority: Can defer - workaround is simple (restart app)
title: Recreate file watcher when project changes

description:
Allow users to paste screenshots (Ctrl+V / Cmd+V) from the clipboard directly into the chat input area.

## User story
User copies a screenshot, pastes into the chat text box, sees a thumbnail preview, sends the message — the agent receives and can reason about the image.

## Key findings
- Claude CLI currently receives prompts as a **positional CLI argument**, not via stdin stream-json. No --input-format stream-json is used today.
- Two implementation paths:

### Option A: Temp file (simpler, no protocol change)
1. Frontend: listen for paste events, extract image/png or image/jpeg from clipboardData.items
2. Show inline thumbnail preview in the input area
3. On send: Tauri command writes base64 to ~/.bp6/sessions/<bead_id>/attachments/<uuid>.png (same tree as session JSONL logs — kept as evidence for process improvement review)
4. Append path reference to the message text so Claude can read it
5. Claude uses its Read tool to load and view the image
- Con: relies on Claude proactively reading the path

### Option B: Switch to --input-format stream-json (proper)
1. Add --input-format stream-json to CLI invocation args
2. Pipe structured JSON message (with image content block) via stdin instead of positional arg
3. Frontend sends base64 image data to Tauri; Tauri includes it in the JSON message
- Pro: first-class image support, same as API
- Con: requires changing the message-send protocol for ALL sessions (higher risk)

## Recommended approach
Option A for a quick win, with Option B as a follow-up if image reasoning quality is poor.

## Image storage location
Images saved to ~/.bp6/sessions/<bead_id>/attachments/<session_id>-<uuid>.png
This co-locates attachments with session JSONL logs so they are available for process improvement review.
For untracked sessions: ~/.bp6/sessions/untracked/attachments/

## Frontend work (both options)
- Detect paste event with image data in ChatDialog.tsx input area
- Render thumbnail preview with remove button
- Pass image state through to the send-message handler

## Needs investigation
- Confirm Claude Code actually reads image files passed by path (test manually)
- Check if --input-format stream-json is compatible with --resume (session continuity)
title: Paste clipboard images into chat input

## Overview
Implement a new 'Customer' AI persona that represents the system end-user/beneficiary perspective. This persona facilitates exploratory conversations about project scope, requirements, and priorities from a customer/stakeholder lens.

## Behavior Modes

### 1. Bootstrap Mode (No Epics Exist)
When the project has no epics, the Customer persona guides an open-ended discovery conversation:

**Discovery Questions:**
- What is the core idea/mission of this project?
- Who are the key stakeholders and their roles?
- What problems are we solving for end users?
- What are the success criteria and business goals?
- What are the key user journeys or workflows?
- What constraints exist (budget, timeline, technical, regulatory)?

**Output:**
- Helps crystallize the vision and scope
- Identifies core value propositions
- Suggests potential epics based on conversation
- Documents key decisions and assumptions

### 2. Refinement Mode (Epics Exist)
When epics exist, the Customer persona reads the current scope and facilitates:

**Scope Conversations:**
- **Refinement**: Clarify requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases
- **Addition**: Identify gaps, missing features, new opportunities
- **Removal**: Challenge scope creep, deprioritize low-value work
- **Validation**: Ensure work aligns with end-user needs
- **Prioritization**: Discuss trade-offs from customer perspective

**Contextual Understanding:**
- Reads all existing epics before engaging
- Understands current project state and direction
- References specific epics in conversation
- Suggests connections between features

## Integration Points

### Navigation Bar Button
- Add 'Customer' button to Navigation component (bert-viz/src/components/layout/Navigation.tsx)
- Icon: User or MessageCircle
- Color: Distinctive from other personas (suggest purple/violet)
- Position: Prominent placement for easy access
- **No bead context required** - this persona is project-scoped, not issue-scoped

### Template System
Create templates at:
- `personas/customer/chat.md` - Main conversation template
- `personas/customer/bootstrap.md` - Bootstrap mode specific guidance
- `personas/customer/refinement.md` - Refinement mode with epic context

### Context Loading
The Customer persona should:
- Automatically detect if epics exist in the project
- Load all epic titles, descriptions, and metadata for context
- Switch behavior based on bootstrap vs. refinement mode
- Maintain conversation history for iterative refinement

## Expert Consultant Approach
The Customer persona acts as an experienced product consultant who:
- Asks probing questions to uncover hidden requirements
- Challenges assumptions constructively
- Thinks holistically about user experience
- Balances business value with technical feasibility
- Focuses on outcomes over outputs
- Uses Socratic method to guide thinking

## Implementation Tasks
1. Create CustomerPersona plugin in Rust (PersonaPlugin trait)
2. Implement epic detection and loading logic
3. Create conversation templates for both modes
4. Add Navigation bar button with proper routing
5. Wire up persona to agent session system
6. Test both bootstrap and refinement scenarios

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Navigation button launches Customer persona session
- [ ] Bootstrap mode works in empty projects
- [ ] Refinement mode loads and references existing epics
- [ ] Conversations feel natural and consultative
- [ ] Can iteratively refine scope through multiple sessions
- [ ] Persona integrates with existing beads workflow

### Button Placement
Add to Navigation component alongside existing persona buttons:
- Location: bert-viz/src/components/layout/Navigation.tsx
- Position: After specialist buttons, before settings
- Label: 'Customer' or 'Customer Voice'
- Icon: User or UserCircle from lucide-react
- Color scheme: bg-purple-600 hover:bg-purple-700 (distinct from other personas)

### Click Handler
```typescript
onClick={() => onOpenChat('customer', 'chat', undefined, undefined)}
```

Key differences from other personas:
- No beadId required (project-scoped, not issue-scoped)
- No role required (Customer is not a specialist)
- Always uses 'chat' task (no decompose/implement variants)

### Visual Design
- Use distinct color to emphasize customer-centric nature
- Consider adding tooltip: 'Explore scope and requirements from customer perspective'
- Ensure button is always visible (not hidden behind dropdown)

## Backend Persona Plugin

### Rust Implementation
File: bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/personas/customer.rs

```rust
pub struct CustomerPersona;

impl PersonaPlugin for CustomerPersona {
    fn get_system_prompt(&self, context: &AgentContext) -> Result<String> {
        // Detect bootstrap vs refinement mode
        let epics_exist = context.project.has_epics()?;
        
        let template_name = if epics_exist {
            "refinement"
        } else {
            "bootstrap"
        };
        
        // Load base template + mode-specific template
        let base = load_template("personas/customer/chat.md", context)?;
        let mode_template = load_template(
            &format!("personas/customer/{}.md", template_name), 
            context
        )?;
        
        Ok(format!("{}\n\n{}", base, mode_template))
    }
}
```

### Epic Loading Logic
For refinement mode, preload epic context:
```rust
fn load_epic_context(context: &AgentContext) -> Result<String> {
    let epics = context.project.get_all_epics()?;
    
    let mut epic_summary = String::from("# Current Project Scope\n\n");
    for epic in epics {
        epic_summary.push_str(&format!(
            "## {} - {}\n{}\n\n",
            epic.id, epic.title, epic.description
        ));
    }
    
    epic_summary
}
```

## Template Structure

### Base Template (personas/customer/chat.md)
- Define Customer persona identity and role
- Establish conversational tone (consultative, curious, outcome-focused)
- Core question frameworks for discovery

### Bootstrap Template (personas/customer/bootstrap.md)
- Specific prompts for greenfield projects
- Vision and mission discovery
- Stakeholder identification
- Success criteria definition

### Refinement Template (personas/customer/refinement.md)
- Epic analysis framework
- Gap identification questions
- Prioritization discussion guides

description:
## Observed Behavior
1. Start first chat session (Epic A) → SessionList shows 1 session ✅
2. Navigate to different epic (Epic B) 
3. Start second chat session → SessionList goes blank, shows 0 sessions ❌

## Evidence: Sessions DO Exist
```
~/.bp6/sessions/bp6-643/552a3adb-545a-42e0-87e7-6081e05b1f68-1771067225.jsonl
~/.bp6/sessions/bp6-j33p/fe6233b2-cf91-494b-9026-7df9e2897352-1771067238.jsonl
```
✅ Both session files exist on disk
✅ Sessions are running in backend
❌ SessionList UI shows empty

## Root Cause
**The Rust backend is returning/emitting empty session list** when it should return both sessions.

When the second session is created:
1. `start_agent_session()` creates new session ✅
2. Session stored in SESSIONS HashMap ✅  
3. Session file written to disk ✅
4. `emit_session_list_changed()` is called
5. **BUG**: It reads SESSIONS HashMap and gets [] or wrong data ❌
6. Emits empty array to frontend
7. SessionList receives [] and updates UI to show "No active sessions"

## Investigation Focus

### Primary Suspect: `emit_session_list_changed()` 
**File**: `bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs:614`

Check:
- [ ] Does it correctly read ALL sessions from SESSIONS HashMap?
- [ ] Is there a lock/race condition when reading while writing?
- [ ] Is the filter for `status == Running` working correctly?
- [ ] Is SessionInfo serialization correct after camelCase reversion?

### Secondary: `list_active_sessions()` command
**File**: `bert-viz/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`

Check:
- [ ] Does it read from the same SESSIONS HashMap?
- [ ] Same filtering/serialization logic?

## Likely Bugs (Prioritized)

### 🔴 Most Likely
**Lock/read issue**: When second session is created, emit_session_list_changed() reads SESSIONS before the new session is fully written, OR while holding a lock that prevents reading.

### 🟡 Possible  
**Status not set**: Sessions created but status != SessionStatus::Running, so they're filtered out.

### 🟢 Less Likely
**Serialization**: SessionInfo struct fields don't match TypeScript interface after camelCase changes.

## Debug Steps
1. Add debug logging to `emit_session_list_changed()`:
   ```rust
   let sessions = SESSIONS.read().unwrap();
   println!("DEBUG: SESSIONS count: {}", sessions.len());
   for (id, state) in sessions.iter() {
       println!("  - {} status: {:?}", id, state.status);
   }
   ```

2. Check if sessions have correct status when created
3. Verify emit is called with non-empty vec
4. Check TypeScript console for received event payload

## Expected Fix
Ensure `emit_session_list_changed()` correctly reads and emits ALL running sessions from the HashMap, not just the newly created one.
notes:
## Implementation

Modified `emit_session_list_changed()` in bert-viz/src-tauri/src/agent/session.rs:243-251

Changed from:
```rust
let _ = app_handle.emit("session-list-changed", session_list);
```

To:
```rust
let _ = app_handle.emit("session-list-changed", serde_json::json!({ "sessions": session_list }));
```

This ensures the event payload matches the TypeScript interface expectation.

## Testing

- ✅ Rust compilation successful (`cargo check`)
- Frontend expects: `{ sessions: SessionInfo[] }`
- Backend now emits: `{ sessions: SessionInfo[] }`
- Payload structure now matches
title: Blank/broken screen when selecting second session

notes:
Current issues:
- Complex absolute positioning + flex + justify-end causing layout bugs
- Session switching triggers layout recalculation issues  
- HTML content from markdown breaks flex calculations
- Multiple wrapper divs and refs make code hard to maintain

- Use standard flex-col layout, no absolute positioning
- Reverse flex-direction for bottom-anchored chat

description:
File watcher doesn't detect changes when using beads-sync branch worktree setup.

Current Issue:
- find_beads_file() correctly locates worktree path: .git/beads-worktrees/beads-sync/.beads/issues.jsonl
- But file watcher events don't trigger UI updates
- Line 503-505 only compares filenames, not full paths

Root Cause:
The affects_target check only compares file_name():
```rust
let affects_target = event.paths.iter().any(|p|
    p.file_name() == watch_target.file_name()
);
```

This should compare the full canonical path instead.

Proposed Fix:
```rust
let affects_target = event.paths.iter().any(|p|
    p.canonicalize().ok() == watch_target.canonicalize().ok() ||
    p == &watch_target
);
```

Or simpler:
```rust  
let affects_target = event.paths.iter().any(|p| p == &watch_target);
```

Acceptance Criteria:
- UI updates when issues.jsonl changes in worktree
- No false positives from other issues.jsonl files
- Works for both local and sync-branch modes
title: Fix file watcher for beads-sync worktree paths
